principle: WCAG 2.2 §2.4.7 Focus Visible / NN/g #3 User control & freedom / Apple HIG modal-sheet on-screen affordance
location: /projects → PLANNER → COVERAGE heat-sink grid → gap-fill popover ([role=dialog].gap-fill-sheet)
problem: Tapping an UPPER-viewport heat-sink grid cell (cell 0 at y=0) opens the gap-fill popover with role=dialog. Measured getBoundingClientRect: top = -305px at 375 (top = -348px at 414). The header and the 44x44 'Close gap-fill popover' x button render at top = -297px / -339px — fully ABOVE the viewport, off-screen and not tappable. The element DOES carry the .gap-fill-sheet class AND the @media (max-width:767px) .gap-fill-sheet rule IS in the stylesheet (top:auto !important; bottom:calc(60px+safe-area) !important; left/right:0.5rem !important). But computed top resolves to -305px anyway: the !important bottom-sheet rule is being beaten in the cascade, so the popover still positions like an anchored desktop popover relative to the tapped cell. The header + close are off the top of the screen. A backdrop exists (tap-to-dismiss works) so the user is not fully trapped, but the documented fix criterion — header + x ON-SCREEN with top >= 0 — is NOT met. The Tailwind-v4 important-syntax trap that broke the prior two attempts is still effectively winning.
fix: The .gap-fill-sheet !important rule is present but not winning for the `top` property at mobile. Root cause to confirm: a same-or-higher-specificity declaration (Tailwind utility on the element, e.g. a `top-*` / `inset-*` util, or a JS-computed style applied via CSSOM with priority) overrides it. Concrete fixes, in order of robustness: (1) Remove ALL top/inset utility classes from the dialog element at the mobile breakpoint — gate the desktop anchoring utilities behind `md:` only (md:top-full md:left-1/2 etc.) and ensure NO base/un-prefixed top utility leaks to mobile. (2) Render a structurally SEPARATE bottom-sheet element at <768 (conditional on a matchMedia/useMediaQuery hook) rather than re-styling the desktop popover — this avoids the cascade fight entirely and is the most reliable. (3) If keeping one element, set positioning in inline style via JS at <768 (style.top='auto'; style.bottom='calc(60px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom,0px))'; style.left/right='0.5rem') because inline style beats stylesheet !important and beats Tailwind utilities. Verify after: tap cell index 0 at 375 and assert dialog.getBoundingClientRect().top >= 0 and the close button top >= 0.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §1.4.10 Reflow (no horizontal scroll at 320 CSS px / responsive) / Refactoring UI responsive layout / Jakob's Law
location: /library — desktop sidebar + multi-column table layout activating at the md (768px) breakpoint
problem: At 375 and 414 /library is clean (scrollWidth == clientWidth) in BOTH grid and list views, with owned (circle) + wanted (star) toggles fully on-screen at 44x44. BUT at 768 BOTH views overflow: documentElement.scrollWidth = 922 vs clientWidth = 753 (169px horizontal overflow, page-level horizontal scrollbar visible). Cause: the `md:` breakpoint = 768px switches the WHOLE app to the DESKTOP layout — a ~200px left sidebar (MINI MANAGER / nav / 'V0.1.0 // STABLE' footer) PLUS the desktop multi-column paint table appear simultaneously. The desktop list rows use `md:contents` so the per-row action buttons (Mark as owned/wanted) break out of the `.caret-row overflow-hidden` clamp and extend to right=926px. The desktop table assumes full desktop width but only has 753px of content area (viewport 768 minus the 200px sidebar minus scrollbar), so columns collide (BRAND / LINE+NAME headers literally overlap as 'LINGNEK') and the owned/wanted columns are pushed off the right edge. This is a tablet breakpoint collision: desktop chrome turns on too early for the space available.
fix: Push the desktop sidebar + desktop table layout from the `md:` (768) breakpoint to `lg:` (1024) so 768px tablets keep the mobile/no-sidebar layout that already passes. In Tailwind terms: change the layout shell and the /library row component's `md:` prefixes that enable the sidebar and the `md:contents` table-row mode to `lg:`. Alternatively, if the desktop layout must stay at 768: constrain the table content area to the actual available width (the table/row container must respect `max-width:100%` and `overflow-x:hidden`, and the desktop row grid must use `minmax(0,1fr)` / `min-w-0` columns so action buttons stay inside the 753px content area instead of overflowing to 926px). Verify after: at 768, both grid and list views, assert documentElement.scrollWidth == clientWidth.

principle: NN/g #1 Visibility of system status (returning users must get the fresh build) / cache-busting correctness
location: Service worker /sw.js — BUILD_ID stamp on Vercel production
problem: FAIL. The live shell cache name is `mm-shell-dev`, NOT `mm-shell-<sha>`. Confirmed reproducibly: after unregister + clear, the freshly registered SW recreated `mm-shell-dev` (and `caches.keys()` returns ['mm-shell-dev'] on every reload). Root cause is in the live /sw.js source: `const BUILD_ID = "__BUILD_ID__".startsWith("__") ? "dev" : "__BUILD_ID__";`. The literal token `__BUILD_ID__` was NEVER replaced by the build-time stamp script on this Vercel deploy, so `.startsWith("__")` is true and BUILD_ID falls back to "dev". The per-deploy cache-versioning logic (SHELL_CACHE = `mm-shell-${BUILD_ID}`, activate deletes non-KEEP caches, skipWaiting + clients.claim) is all correct in source — but because BUILD_ID is permanently 'dev', the cache name never changes between deploys, so the exact returning-user-stale-shell problem UX-1505 set out to fix is NOT actually fixed in production. Returning users can still be stranded behind a fixed-name cache.
fix: The stamp/replace step is not running (or not matching) in the Vercel build. Fix the build pipeline so the `__BUILD_ID__` token in sw.js is replaced at build time with `process.env.VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA` (with a timestamp fallback). Concrete: add/repair a postbuild (or prebuild-of-public) script — e.g. a Node script that reads public/sw.js (or the source sw before it lands in the build output that Vercel serves), replaces `__BUILD_ID__` with `(process.env.VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA || Date.now().toString())`, and writes it to the served output path. Ensure it runs in the Vercel build command (the script likely runs in local `next build` but not in the Vercel deploy, or it writes to a path Vercel does not serve from). Verify after deploy: fetch /sw.js and assert it does NOT contain the literal `__BUILD_ID__`, and that caches.keys() on the live site returns `mm-shell-<7+ hex chars>`, not `mm-shell-dev`.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum, 24x24) — dense data-viz exception noted
problem: Each heat-sink/coverage grid cell is 21x21px, below the WCAG 2.2 §2.5.8 24x24 CSS-px minimum. This is a dense hue-sorted spectrum data-viz (7,144 cells), which can qualify for the §2.5.8 'essential'/spacing exception, and tapping opens an equivalent gap-fill action. Flagging for awareness, not as a launch blocker.
fix: Acceptable as a dense data-viz under the §2.5.8 exception. Optionally bump cells to 24x24 in 'Full' density, or rely on the existing Condensed/Full toggle as the spacing accommodation. No launch-blocking action required.
